# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Prefer these Hugging Face tools over web search for live Hub data; start with hf_fs.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'smaschek'

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## plugin:browser-use:browser-use
# This MCP server

These rules override the skill below where they differ:
- Code runs in browser_exec; there is no shell, so ignore `BU_NAME=... browser-use <<'PY'` examples.
- Local: without a cloud browser, browser_exec drives the user's own Chrome; where none can be attached (no Chrome installed, Linux with no display, or remote debugging off in Chrome) its own Chromium on a temp profile instead. The first browser_exec result says which, and how to get the user's Chrome.
- Cloud: `start_remote_daemon()` (call browser_login first if not signed in). Every later browser_exec and
  browser_screenshot drives that cloud browser; never pass BU_NAME. One cloud browser per server, under a name only it
  uses: a name passed to start_remote_daemon / stop_remote_daemon is ignored.
- It lives 30 minutes unless you pass `timeout=<minutes>` (up to 240), and this server stops it when it
  exits. Once it ends, calls fail with an error: start a new one, never fall back to the local Chrome.
- Code runs in this server's process: it can read the server's environment (BROWSER_USE_API_KEY when set) and files.
- The live view and CDP URLs grant control of the browser, so they are not shown. Only if the user asks to watch, run
  `os.environ["BH_OPEN_LIVE_URL"] = "1"` before start_remote_daemon: the live view then opens in their browser, and
  both are returned.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timed-out `scroll(...)` on an attached background tab is evide… [truncated]

1	# SMA-819: drop empty text blocks in the Anthropic translator
2	
3	Status: revised after the spec challenge, 2026-11-20. Size: a small change.
4	
5	## Intent
6	
7	The Anthropic translator (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`)
8	sends `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` for an empty user text part. The Messages
9	API probably rejects empty text blocks with HTTP 400. The live check must
10	confirm this. The bad item stays in the session, so each replay of that
11	session fails again.
12	
13	These paths make a blank text part:
14	
15	- an empty user input;
16	- a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])` (PR #346);
17	- whitespace-only text that a model emits, which is then replayed;
18	- a session that another provider recorded.
19	
20	## Goals
21	
22	- The translator drops each `ContentPart::Text` whose `text.trim()` is empty.
23	  The definition of "blank" is Rust `str::trim()` (Unicode `White_Space`). The
24	  design accepts any difference from the API's own definition. This rule applies
25	  to user messages and assistant messages, new and replayed.
26	- The translator does not send a user message or an assistant message that has
27	  no blocks left. This is wider than blank text. It also removes messages that
28	  have only `Reasoning`, only `Audio`, or only unknown parts. Today those go out
29	  as `content: []`.
30	- The translator sends `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks in the order of the
31	  items. The message that removes an empty assistant carrier needs this fix (see
32	  "Ordering fix").
33	- The system text is treated as absent when `system_text.trim()` is empty. This
34	  is a one-line change at `request.rs:106`. It prevents a whitespace-only system
35	  block with `cache_control`.
36	- `build_body` returns `ModelError::Other` before any HTTP call when the
37	  translated `messages` array is empty. The error text is neutral, for example
38	  "no message with content to send (empty and whitespace-only text is not
39	  sent)". The text must also be correct for a request that has only
40	  `Item::System`.
41	
42	## Non-goals
43	
44	- No change to `tool_result` content. The live check records whether the API
45	  accepts an empty `tool_result` string, for information only.
46	- No change to the other providers. The Gemini translator has a related problem
47	  in SMA-820. The Bedrock translator
48	  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`) also
49	  emits blank text. SMA-824 covers it.
50	- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`. Items in the session stay as they are.
51	  The fix is on the wire only.
52	- No support for extended thinking across a tool loop. The translator drops
53	  `Reasoning` on input today, and this ticket does not change that.
54	
55	## Anti-goals
56	
57	- The translator must not put placeholder text in place of a dropped block. That
58	  would send words the user did not write.
59	- The translator must not block a final assistant message that a caller sends on
60	  purpose (a prefill).
61	- The fix must not make a request fail that works on `main` today.
62	
63	## Decisions (from the conversation)
64	
65	1. **Edge case (Sven chose option c, after the spec challenge).** `build_body`
66	   fails early with `ModelError::Other` in two cases:
67	   - the drops leave no messages;
68	   - the last conversation item (`UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `ToolCall`
69	     or `ToolResult`) is a `UserMessage` that the translator dropped, and the
70	     request now ends with an assistant message. An `AssistantMessage` that the
71	     translator also drops after that user message does not count as a later
72	     item, so `user q, assistant a, user "", assistant ""` is rejected. A
73	     dropped assistant item with no dropped user message before it is a caller
74	     prefill and is sent.
75	
76	   A caller that ends the item list with an assistant message on purpose (a
77	   prefill) is not blocked. The translator reports the second case to
78	   `build_body`, for example with a flag on `TranslatedMessages`. Sven first
79	   chose option (b) and changed to (c), because a drop-induced prefill makes
80	   the model continue its old answer.
81	2. **Approach (Sven chose option 1).** Filter where the blocks are made. See
82	   "Approaches".
83	
84	## Approaches
85	
86	1. **Filter where the blocks are made (chosen).** `user_blocks` and
87	   `assistant_blocks` skip blank `Text` parts. The `UserMessage` and
88	   `AssistantMessage` arms do not push a message with no blocks. `build_body`
89	   checks for an empty `messages` array. The rule stays next to the code that
90	   made the problem.
91	2. **A cleanup pass on the finished JSON.** This catches blocks that other code
92	   adds later. But it reads untyped JSON and puts the rule away from the code
93	   that makes the blocks.
94	3. **Filter the `Item` list before translation.** This puts an Anthropic rule in
95	   a generic place and must rebuild `Item` values. It does not fit.
96	
97	## Ordering fix
98	
99	Today an `AssistantMessage` with zero blocks is still pushed as
100	`assistant: []`. A following `Item::ToolCall` folds into it. That hides an
101	ordering bug. When this change removes the empty carrier, the bug shows:
102	
103	```text
104	items: User q, Assistant[Reasoning], ToolCall tu_1, ToolResult tu_1, Assistant "done"
105	bad:   user[q], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[tool_use tu_1], assistant[done]
106	good:  user[q], assistant[tool_use tu_1], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[done]
107	```
108	
109	The same bug is on `main` today for a tool call that has no `AssistantMessage`
110	(`User q, ToolCall, ToolResult, Assistant "done"`). A second form is also on
111	`main`: `ToolCall t2` after a pending `ToolResult r1` folds into the earlier
112	assistant message, before `r1`.
113	
114	The fix has three parts. Together they make the wire order follow the item
115	order:
116	
117	1. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks before pending
118	   `tool_result` blocks. The `System` arm and the end of the loop already use
119	   this order.
120	2. The `ToolCall` arm flushes pending `tool_result` blocks before the fold
121	   check.
122	3. The `ToolResult` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks first.
123	
124	## Behavior details
125	
126	- A `UserMessage` that has pending `tool_result` blocks keeps those blocks when
127	  all its text is blank. The message is sent with only the `tool_result` blocks.
128	  This covers the SMA-804 `Inject([Text ""])` path after a tool result.
129	- When the translator drops an `AssistantMessage`, a following `Item::ToolCall`
130	  folds into the last message if that message is an assistant message, and
131	  goes into `pending_tool_use` if it is not. The ordering fix keeps both cases
132	  correct.
133	- A dropped message can put two messages with the same role next to each other.
134	  The translator already sends two adjacent user messages for two adjacent
135	  `UserMessage` items. The design keeps that behavior and relies on the API to
136	  join the turns. The live check must confirm this.
137	- A text block that is not blank keeps its exact text, with its whitespace. The
138	  translator does not trim the text it sends.
139	- `cache::apply_cache_strategy` runs after the drops, so the `LastTurn` marker
140	  goes on a block that is really sent.
141	
142	## Verification
143	
144	### Live probes (before the code change)
145	
146	The probes need a real key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or Claude through Bedrock or
147	Vertex. A keyless proxy with `mock_response` does not reach Anthropic's
148	validation, so it cannot prove these claims. **If no real key is available,
149	stop and bring this back to Sven.** Record the request bodies and the
150	responses. Never record headers.
151	
152	Use `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` (the IDs in `tests/live.rs`),
153	with thinking off unless the probe says otherwise. The probe bodies are:
154	
155	| # | `messages` | What it proves |
156	|---|------------|----------------|
157	| P1 | `[user [text ""]]` | the 400 for an empty block |
158	| P2 | `[user [text "  \n\t"]]` | the 400 for a whitespace-only block |
159	| P3 | `[user "a", user "b"]` | the API joins adjacent user turns |
160	| P4 | `[user "q", assistant "a1", assistant "a2", user "r"]` | the API joins adjacent assistant turns in the middle |
161	| P5 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure."]` | a final assistant message (a prefill) works |
162	| P6 | P5 with thinking on | a prefill with thinking |
163	| P7 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure.\n"]` | a prefill with trailing whitespace |
164	| P8 | `[assistant "a"]` | an assistant-first request |
165	| P9 | a `tool_result` with content `""` | information only (non-goal) |
166	
167	**Stop conditions.** If P3 or P4 gets a 400, stop and bring it back to Sven
168	before you change the design. If P5, P6, P7 or P8 gets a 400, record it and
169	report it at the next gate. Decision (c) already blocks a drop-induced
170	prefill, so these results are for the record.
171	
172	### Probe results (2026-11-20, real key)
173	
174	| # | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
175	|---|--------------------|---------------------|
176	| P1 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` | 400, same text |
177	| P2 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` | 400, same text |
178	| P3 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
179	| P4 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
180	| P5 | 200 (prefill continued) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` |
181	| P6 | not run | 400, same prefill text |
182	| P7 | 400 `messages: final assistant content cannot end with trailing whitespace` | 400, same text |
183	| P8 | 200 (treated as a prefill) | 400, same prefill text |

# SMA-819: drop empty text blocks in the Anthropic translator

Status: revised after the spec challenge, 2026-11-20. Size: a small change.

## Intent

The Anthropic translator (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs`)
sends `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` for an empty user text part. The Messages
API probably rejects empty text blocks with HTTP 400. The live check must
confirm this. The bad item stays in the session, so each replay of that
session fails again.

These paths make a blank text part:

- an empty user input;
- a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])` (PR #346);
- whitespace-only text that a model emits, which is then replayed;
- a session that another provider recorded.

## Goals

- The translator drops each `ContentPart::Text` whose `text.trim()` is empty.
  The definition of "blank" is Rust `str::trim()` (Unicode `White_Space`). The
  design accepts any difference from the API's own definition. This rule applies
  to user messages and assistant messages, new and replayed.
- The translator does not send a user message or an assistant message that has
  no blocks left. This is wider than blank text. It also removes messages that
  have only `Reasoning`, only `Audio`, or only unknown parts. Today those go out
  as `content: []`.
- The translator sends `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks in the order of the
  items. The message that removes an empty assistant carrier needs this fix (see
  "Ordering fix").
- The system text is treated as absent when `system_text.trim()` is empty. This
  is a one-line change at `request.rs:106`. It prevents a whitespace-only system
  block with `cache_control`.
- `build_body` returns `ModelError::Other` before any HTTP call when the
  translated `messages` array is empty. The error text is neutral, for example
  "no message with content to send (empty and whitespace-only text is not
  sent)". The text must also be correct for a request that has only
  `Item::System`.

## Non-goals

- No change to `tool_result` content. The live check records whether the API
  accepts an empty `tool_result` string, for information only.
- No change to the other providers. The Gemini translator has a related problem
  in SMA-820. The Bedrock translator
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/translate/request.rs`) also
  emits blank text. SMA-824 covers it.
- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`. Items in the session stay as they are.
  The fix is on the wire only.
- No support for extended thinking across a tool loop. The translator drops
  `Reasoning` on input today, and this ticket does not change that.

## Anti-goals

- The translator must not put placeholder text in place of a dropped block. That
  would send words the user did not write.
- The translator must not block a final assistant message that a caller sends on
  purpose (a prefill).
- The fix must not make a request fail that works on `main` today.

## Decisions (from the conversation)

1. **Edge case (Sven chose option c, after the spec challenge).** `build_body`
   fails early with `ModelError::Other` in two cases:
   - the drops leave no messages;
   - the last conversation item (`UserMessage`, `AssistantMessage`, `ToolCall`
     or `ToolResult`) is a `UserMessage` that the translator dropped, and the
     request now ends with an assistant message. An `AssistantMessage` that the
     translator also drops after that user message does not count as a later
     item, so `user q, assistant a, user "", assistant ""` is rejected. A
     dropped assistant item with no dropped user message before it is a caller
     prefill and is sent.

   A caller that ends the item list with an assistant message on purpose (a
   prefill) is not blocked. The translator reports the second case to
   `build_body`, for example with a flag on `TranslatedMessages`. Sven first
   chose option (b) and changed to (c), because a drop-induced prefill makes
   the model continue its old answer.
2. **Approach (Sven chose option 1).** Filter where the blocks are made. See
   "Approaches".

## Approaches

1. **Filter where the blocks are made (chosen).** `user_blocks` and
   `assistant_blocks` skip blank `Text` parts. The `UserMessage` and
   `AssistantMessage` arms do not push a message with no blocks. `build_body`
   checks for an empty `messages` array. The rule stays next to the code that
   made the problem.
2. **A cleanup pass on the finished JSON.** This catches blocks that other code
   adds later. But it reads untyped JSON and puts the rule away from the code
   that makes the blocks.
3. **Filter the `Item` list before translation.** This puts an Anthropic rule in
   a generic place and must rebuild `Item` values. It does not fit.

## Ordering fix

Today an `AssistantMessage` with zero blocks is still pushed as
`assistant: []`. A following `Item::ToolCall` folds into it. That hides an
ordering bug. When this change removes the empty carrier, the bug shows:

```text
items: User q, Assistant[Reasoning], ToolCall tu_1, ToolResult tu_1, Assistant "done"
bad:   user[q], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[tool_use tu_1], assistant[done]
good:  user[q], assistant[tool_use tu_1], user[tool_result tu_1], assistant[done]
```

The same bug is on `main` today for a tool call that has no `AssistantMessage`
(`User q, ToolCall, ToolResult, Assistant "done"`). A second form is also on
`main`: `ToolCall t2` after a pending `ToolResult r1` folds into the earlier
assistant message, before `r1`.

The fix has three parts. Together they make the wire order follow the item
order:

1. The `AssistantMessage` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks before pending
   `tool_result` blocks. The `System` arm and the end of the loop already use
   this order.
2. The `ToolCall` arm flushes pending `tool_result` blocks before the fold
   check.
3. The `ToolResult` arm flushes pending `tool_use` blocks first.

## Behavior details

- A `UserMessage` that has pending `tool_result` blocks keeps those blocks when
  all its text is blank. The message is sent with only the `tool_result` blocks.
  This covers the SMA-804 `Inject([Text ""])` path after a tool result.
- When the translator drops an `AssistantMessage`, a following `Item::ToolCall`
  folds into the last message if that message is an assistant message, and
  goes into `pending_tool_use` if it is not. The ordering fix keeps both cases
  correct.
- A dropped message can put two messages with the same role next to each other.
  The translator already sends two adjacent user messages for two adjacent
  `UserMessage` items. The design keeps that behavior and relies on the API to
  join the turns. The live check must confirm this.
- A text block that is not blank keeps its exact text, with its whitespace. The
  translator does not trim the text it sends.
- `cache::apply_cache_strategy` runs after the drops, so the `LastTurn` marker
  goes on a block that is really sent.

## Verification

### Live probes (before the code change)

The probes need a real key: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or Claude through Bedrock or
Vertex. A keyless proxy with `mock_response` does not reach Anthropic's
validation, so it cannot prove these claims. **If no real key is available,
stop and bring this back to Sven.** Record the request bodies and the
responses. Never record headers.

Use `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` (the IDs in `tests/live.rs`),
with thinking off unless the probe says otherwise. The probe bodies are:

| # | `messages` | What it proves |
|---|------------|----------------|
| P1 | `[user [text ""]]` | the 400 for an empty block |
| P2 | `[user [text "  \n\t"]]` | the 400 for a whitespace-only block |
| P3 | `[user "a", user "b"]` | the API joins adjacent user turns |
| P4 | `[user "q", assistant "a1", assistant "a2", user "r"]` | the API joins adjacent assistant turns in the middle |
| P5 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure."]` | a final assistant message (a prefill) works |
| P6 | P5 with thinking on | a prefill with thinking |
| P7 | `[user "q", assistant "Sure.\n"]` | a prefill with trailing whitespace |
| P8 | `[assistant "a"]` | an assistant-first request |
| P9 | a `tool_result` with content `""` | information only (non-goal) |

**Stop conditions.** If P3 or P4 gets a 400, stop and bring it back to Sven
before you change the design. If P5, P6, P7 or P8 gets a 400, record it and
report it at the next gate. Decision (c) already blocks a drop-induced
prefill, so these results are for the record.

### Probe results (2026-11-20, real key)

| # | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
|---|--------------------|---------------------|
| P1 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` | 400, same text |
| P2 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` | 400, same text |
| P3 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
| P4 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
| P5 | 200 (prefill continued) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` |
| P6 | not run | 400, same prefill text |
| P7 | 400 `messages: final assistant content cannot end with trailing whitespace` | 400, same text |
| P8 | 200 (treated as a prefill) | 400, same prefill text |
| P9 | 200 | not run |

No stop condition fired. P3 and P4 confirm the reliance on joined turns. P5,
P6 and P8 confirm decision (c): on newer models a drop-induced prefill is a
400, and on older models it continues the old answer.

### Live tests (after the fix)

Add `#[ignore]` tests to `tests/live.rs`. Record the output of a real run in
the PR. A skipped run does not count. The cases are:

- (a) user, assistant with `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, blank user. This is the
  SMA-804 path.
- (b) case (a) with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn`.
- (c) user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant text,
  user. This is the ordering path.
- (d) user, assistant, blank user, real user. This is the replay path.

### Unit tests in `translate/request.rs`

Compare the full `messages` array with `assert_eq!`, not only lengths.

- `empty_text_part_is_emitted_as_empty_block` changes to assert that the block
  is dropped. Rename it to match.
- Whitespace-only text (`"  \n\t"`) is dropped.
- A user message with no blocks left is not sent.
- A user message with blank text and pending tool results keeps the
  `tool_result` blocks.
- Blank assistant text is dropped, and an assistant message with no blocks left
  is not sent.
- A reasoning-only assistant message is not sent.
- A replayed sequence (real user, assistant, blank user, real user) keeps only
  the real messages.
- Ordering: user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant
  text.
- Ordering: the same with whitespace assistant text.
- Ordering: a tool call with no `AssistantMessage`, then a `ToolResult`, then
  assistant text. This pins the bug that is on `main`.
- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending `ToolResult` does not fold into the
  earlier assistant message.
- Fold target: a blank assistant after a kept assistant, then a `ToolCall`.
- A whitespace-only system text gives no `system` field.

### Tests for `build_body` and `invoke`

- `build_body` with only a blank user message returns `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with only `Item::System` returns `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with `Item::System` and a blank user message returns
  `ModelError::Other`.
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user ""]` returns
  `ModelError::Other` (decision c).
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user "", assistant "b"]` sends
  the request. The caller ended the list with an assistant message.
- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", ToolCall, ToolResult, user ""]`
  sends the request. The `tool_result` blocks make a user message.
- `build_body` with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn` and a trailing blank user message
  puts the marker on the previous real block, and no block has blank text.
- A wiremock test through `invoke` with `.expect(0)`: a blank-only request
  returns `Err` and sends no HTTP request.

## Settled at Gate 1

1. Decision 1 is option (c). See "Decisions".
2. All three parts of the ordering fix are in SMA-819. Two parts are on `main`
   today, but the change needs them to avoid a regression, and they have the
   same cause.
3. The Bedrock translator gets a separate Linear issue.
4. The live probes use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the repo-root `.env`. Load it
   into the process environment only. Never print it or write it to a file.

## Left to the builder

- The exact error text, within the meaning given above.
- The name of the helper that checks for blank text.
- Whether the translator emits a `tracing::debug!` line when it drops a block.
  If it does, the line contains counts only, never text.

## Documentation

- The crate `README.md` and the mdBook do not describe this translation rule.
  Check both. If nothing describes it, no edit is necessary.
- The fix is a `fix(providers)` change, so release-plz bumps the Anthropic crate
  and the facade as usual. No hand version bump.

174	| # | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
175	|---|--------------------|---------------------|
176	| P1 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must be non-empty` | 400, same text |
177	| P2 | 400 `messages: text content blocks must contain non-whitespace text` | 400, same text |
178	| P3 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
179	| P4 | 200 (turns joined) | 200 |
180	| P5 | 200 (prefill continued) | 400 `This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message.` |
181	| P6 | not run | 400, same prefill text |
182	| P7 | 400 `messages: final assistant content cannot end with trailing whitespace` | 400, same text |
183	| P8 | 200 (treated as a prefill) | 400, same prefill text |
184	| P9 | 200 | not run |
185	
186	No stop condition fired. P3 and P4 confirm the reliance on joined turns. P5,
187	P6 and P8 confirm decision (c): on newer models a drop-induced prefill is a
188	400, and on older models it continues the old answer.
189	
190	### Live tests (after the fix)
191	
192	Add `#[ignore]` tests to `tests/live.rs`. Record the output of a real run in
193	the PR. A skipped run does not count. The cases are:
194	
195	- (a) user, assistant with `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, blank user. This is the
196	  SMA-804 path.
197	- (b) case (a) with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn`.
198	- (c) user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant text,
199	  user. This is the ordering path.
200	- (d) user, assistant, blank user, real user. This is the replay path.
201	
202	### Unit tests in `translate/request.rs`
203	
204	Compare the full `messages` array with `assert_eq!`, not only lengths.
205	
206	- `empty_text_part_is_emitted_as_empty_block` changes to assert that the block
207	  is dropped. Rename it to match.
208	- Whitespace-only text (`"  \n\t"`) is dropped.
209	- A user message with no blocks left is not sent.
210	- A user message with blank text and pending tool results keeps the
211	  `tool_result` blocks.
212	- Blank assistant text is dropped, and an assistant message with no blocks left
213	  is not sent.
214	- A reasoning-only assistant message is not sent.
215	- A replayed sequence (real user, assistant, blank user, real user) keeps only
216	  the real messages.
217	- Ordering: user, reasoning-only assistant, `ToolCall`, `ToolResult`, assistant
218	  text.
219	- Ordering: the same with whitespace assistant text.
220	- Ordering: a tool call with no `AssistantMessage`, then a `ToolResult`, then
221	  assistant text. This pins the bug that is on `main`.
222	- Ordering: a `ToolCall` after a pending `ToolResult` does not fold into the
223	  earlier assistant message.
224	- Fold target: a blank assistant after a kept assistant, then a `ToolCall`.
225	- A whitespace-only system text gives no `system` field.
226	
227	### Tests for `build_body` and `invoke`
228	
229	- `build_body` with only a blank user message returns `ModelError::Other`.
230	- `build_body` with only `Item::System` returns `ModelError::Other`.
231	- `build_body` with `Item::System` and a blank user message returns
232	  `ModelError::Other`.
233	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user ""]` returns
234	  `ModelError::Other` (decision c).
235	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", user "", assistant "b"]` sends
236	  the request. The caller ended the list with an assistant message.
237	- `build_body` with `[user "q", assistant "a", ToolCall, ToolResult, user ""]`
238	  sends the request. The `tool_result` blocks make a user message.
239	- `build_body` with `CacheStrategy::LastTurn` and a trailing blank user message
240	  puts the marker on the previous real block, and no block has blank text.
241	- A wiremock test through `invoke` with `.expect(0)`: a blank-only request
242	  returns `Err` and sends no HTTP request.
243	
244	## Settled at Gate 1
245	
246	1. Decision 1 is option (c). See "Decisions".
247	2. All three parts of the ordering fix are in SMA-819. Two parts are on `main`
248	   today, but the change needs them to avoid a regression, and they have the
249	   same cause.
250	3. The Bedrock translator gets a separate Linear issue.
251	4. The live probes use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the repo-root `.env`. Load it
252	   into the process environment only. Never print it or write it to a file.
253	
254	## Left to the builder
255	
256	- The exact error text, within the meaning given above.
257	- The name of the helper that checks for blank text.
258	- Whether the translator emits a `tracing::debug!` line when it drops a block.
259	  If it does, the line contains counts only, never text.
260	
261	## Documentation
262	
263	- The crate `README.md` and the mdBook do not describe this translation rule.
264	  Check both. If nothing describes it, no edit is necessary.
265	- The fix is a `fix(providers)` change, so release-plz bumps the Anthropic crate
266	  and the facade as usual. No hand version bump.

1	//! Canonical wire-format messages and content blocks.
2	//!
3	//! [`Item`] is the superset of OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses,
4	//! Anthropic Messages, and Bedrock Converse content shapes. Provider crates
5	//! serialize the variant native to their wire format and deserialize the
6	//! variant the provider returns; both round-trip without lossy translation.
7	
8	use schemars::JsonSchema;
9	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
10	
11	/// Canonical wire-format message.
12	///
13	/// `ToolCall` and `ToolResult` mirror OpenAI's sibling "tool" role.
14	/// Anthropic providers emit equivalent [`ContentPart::ToolUse`] and
15	/// [`ContentPart::ToolResult`] blocks nested inside `AssistantMessage` /
16	/// `UserMessage` respectively. Both shapes round-trip cleanly through this
17	/// type.
18	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
19	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
20	#[non_exhaustive]
21	pub enum Item {
22	    /// A user-authored message.
23	    UserMessage {
24	        /// One or more content blocks.
25	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
26	    },
27	    /// An assistant-authored message.
28	    AssistantMessage {
29	        /// One or more content blocks.
30	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
31	        /// Name of the agent that produced this message, when known.
32	        /// `Option` because the wire format can lose attribution (e.g. a
33	        /// raw provider response deserialized without context). The
34	        /// session log keeps `agent: String` because the runner always
35	        /// knows which agent emitted.
36	        #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
37	        agent: Option<String>,
38	    },
39	    /// A system message.
40	    System {
41	        /// One or more content blocks (typically a single `Text` block).
42	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
43	    },
44	    /// OpenAI-style sibling-role tool call.
45	    ToolCall {
46	        /// Provider-assigned call identifier.
47	        call_id: String,
48	        /// Tool name.
49	        name: String,
50	        /// JSON arguments.
51	        args: serde_json::Value,
52	    },
53	    /// OpenAI-style "tool" role response.
54	    ToolResult {
55	        /// Matching call identifier.
56	        call_id: String,
57	        /// One or more content blocks (Anthropic permits text + image inside
58	        /// a tool result).
59	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
60	    },
61	}
62	
63	/// One content block inside an [`Item`].
64	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
65	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
66	#[non_exhaustive]
67	pub enum ContentPart {
68	    /// Plain text.
69	    Text {
70	        /// The text payload.
71	        text: String,
72	    },
73	    /// An image, by URL or inline base64.
74	    Image {
75	        /// Where the image bytes come from.
76	        source: MediaSource,
77	    },
78	    /// Audio, by URL or inline base64.
79	    Audio {
80	        /// Where the audio bytes come from.
81	        source: MediaSource,
82	    },
83	    /// Anthropic-style tool_use block nested inside an `AssistantMessage`.
84	    /// Equivalent to a top-level [`Item::ToolCall`].
85	    ToolUse {
86	        /// Provider-assigned call identifier.
87	        call_id: String,
88	        /// Tool name.
89	        name: String,
90	        /// JSON arguments.
91	        args: serde_json::Value,
92	    },
93	    /// Anthropic-style tool_result block nested inside a `UserMessage`.
94	    /// Equivalent to a top-level [`Item::ToolResult`]. The inner content is
95	    /// itself a `Vec<ContentPart>` because Anthropic permits text + image
96	    /// blocks inside a tool_result.
97	    ToolResult {
98	        /// Matching call identifier.
99	        call_id: String,
100	        /// Content blocks comprising the tool's output.
101	        content: Vec<ContentPart>,
102	    },
103	    /// Provider-emitted reasoning trace (e.g. Anthropic extended thinking,
104	    /// OpenAI reasoning summaries).
105	    Reasoning {
106	        /// The reasoning text payload.
107	        text: String,
108	    },
109	}
110	
111	/// Source of a multimedia content block.
112	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
113	#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
114	#[non_exhaustive]
115	pub enum MediaSource {
116	    /// Remote URL.
117	    Url {
118	        /// Absolute URL of the media resource.
119	        url: String,
120	    },
121	    /// Inline base64-encoded bytes.
122	    Base64 {
123	        /// IANA media type (e.g. `image/png`, `audio/wav`).
124	        mime_type: String,
125	        /// Base64-encoded payload.
126	        data: String,
127	    },
128	}

20	It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
21	already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.
22	
23	## Goals
24	
25	- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
26	  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
27	  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
28	  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
29	  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
30	  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
31	- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
32	  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
33	- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
34	  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
35	    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
36	  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
37	    block.
38	
39	  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
40	  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
41	  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
42	  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.
43	
44	  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
45	  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
46	- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
47	  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
48	  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
49	  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
50	  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
51	  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
52	  does not change. No other result moves.
53	- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
54	  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
55	  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
56	  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
57	  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
58	  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.
59	
60	## Non-goals
61	
62	- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
63	- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
64	  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
65	- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
66	  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
67	  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
68	- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.
69	
70	## Anti-goals
71	
72	- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
73	  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
74	  started.
75	- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
76	- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).
77	
78	## Approaches
79	
80	1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
81	   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
82	   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
83	   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
84	   scan valid for old and new logs.
85	2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
86	   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
87	   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
88	   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
89	3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
90	   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.

It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.

## Goals

- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
    block.

  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.

  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
  does not change. No other result moves.
- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.

## Non-goals

- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.

## Anti-goals

- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
  started.
- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).

## Approaches

1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
   scan valid for old and new logs.
2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.

Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-20.

20	It contains SMA-803. So the deny and the old log layout (late transfer result) are
21	already in a release, and sessions with the old layout can exist.
22	
23	## Goals
24	
25	- G1. The parent emits a `ToolOutputItem` for each transfer call of the handoff response.
26	  The stored log of a handoff run is then:
27	  `[AssistantMessage]` `ToolCalled(t)` [`ToolCalled(u)` …] `HandoffOccurred`
28	  `ToolReturned(t)` [`ToolReturned(u)` …] … child events.
29	  `HandoffOccurred` projects to no item. So in the projected conversation the results come
30	  directly after the transfer calls of the same response, in call order.
31	- G2. Remove the SMA-803 deny for a repeated call id. A handoff child can defer a call
32	  that has the same call id as a transfer call above it, at any depth.
33	- G3. Tests check the adjacency on two levels:
34	  - **Stored log:** between a transfer `ToolCalled` and its `ToolReturned`, only
35	    `HandoffOccurred` and the other transfer calls and results of the same response occur.
36	  - **Projection:** every `ToolCall` has its `ToolResult` in the same contiguous tool
37	    block.
38	
39	  Limit: under `ParallelAgent`, branch events interleave live (`workflow.rs`). The parent
40	  awaits `OnHandoff` between `ToolCallItem(t)` and `ToolOutputItem(t)`, so a sibling
41	  branch's items can be recorded between them. This is already true today for every tool
42	  call in a parallel branch. G3 applies to runs without `ParallelAgent`.
43	
44	  Sven accepted on 2026-11-20 that "next to it" means next to it in the projected
45	  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
46	- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
47	  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
48	  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
49	  the transfer text. A session stored before SMA-810 (any earlier core version) then
50	  projects as a new-layout session, with the exceptions listed in the G4 design. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
51	  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
52	  does not change. No other result moves.
53	- G5. **AG-UI call state and AG-UI id per call occurrence** (added at Gate 1
54	  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
55	  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
56	  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
57	  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
58	  mapper must give each call occurrence its own state and its own AG-UI id.
59	
60	## Non-goals
61	
62	- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.
63	- The child transcript does not change. `thread_handoff_transcript` still drops all tool
64	  items, so the child never sees the transfer call or its result.
65	- Non-transfer calls in a handoff response stay out of scope. `transition()` drops them
66	  from the events, so the session does not record them. Their `ToolCallDelta`s can still
67	  reach AG-UI as START/ARGS with no result. This is not caused by this change.
68	- No change to the Temporal driver. It does not support handoffs.
69	
70	## Anti-goals
71	
72	- AG1. A "transferred" result for a handoff that did not occur. The result must come only
73	  after `OnHandoff` permits the handoff, the target agent is known, and the target run
74	  started.
75	- AG2. A change that breaks the resume of a session that core 0.6.0 stored (old layout).
76	- AG3. A second result for a transfer call (for example on a resumed run).
77	
78	## Approaches
79	
80	1. **Emit the result after `HandoffItem`, in the handoff arm of `agent.rs` (chosen).**
81	   The result comes after the `OnHandoff` veto, the depth check and the target lookup.
82	   `transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`) scans back from `HandoffOccurred` over
83	   `ToolCalled` and `AssistantMessage` only. A result after `HandoffOccurred` keeps this
84	   scan valid for old and new logs.
85	2. Emit the result in `transition()`. Pure and easy to unit-test, but it runs before the
86	   `OnHandoff` veto and the target check, and it puts the result before
87	   `HandoffOccurred`, which breaks `transfer_calls_before`. It also writes a result before
88	   a swarm can drop the handoff. Rejected.
89	3. Fix only `SessionRecorder` (write a result on `HandoffItem`). The live event stream
90	   keeps the orphan call, so AG-UI clients still see a call with no result. Rejected.
91	
92	Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-20.
93	
94	## Design
95	
96	### Emission (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs`, `NextAction::Handoff` arm)
97	
98	The event order of a successful handoff becomes:
99	
100	1. `ToolCallItem` for each transfer call (from `transition()`, unchanged).
101	2. Depth check, target lookup, `OnHandoff` (unchanged). A failure ends the run as today.
102	3. `HandoffItem { from, to }` (unchanged).
103	4. `target_agent.run(child, input)` is awaited. This only builds the child stream; it
104	   yields no event. (Today this call comes after step 6. Moving it earlier changes no
105	   observable order, because it emits nothing.)
106	5. **New:** one `ToolOutputItem` per transfer call, in the order of the `ToolCallItem`
107	   events.
108	   - On `Ok`: the first transfer call (the call that names the target) gets
109	     `transferred to {target}`. Each other transfer call of the same response gets
110	     `transfer not performed: this response already transferred to {target}`.
111	   - On `Err`: every transfer call gets `transfer failed: {target} did not start`, and
112	     the run ends with `RunFailed` as today. The text does not include the error, because
113	     the result goes to a model and the error can hold internal detail.
114	6. `AgentUpdated { agent: target }` (on `Ok` only), then the child events.
115	
116	The content of each result is one `ContentPart::Text`. The parent does not push the
117	results into its own `conversation`: after the handoff arm, the parent only re-yields
118	child events and returns, so that state is never read.
119	
120	The transfer call ids are the ids that `agent.rs` already collects as
121	`transfer_call_ids` from the `ToolCallItem` events of the handoff transition.
122	
123	The early exits in step 2 (depth exceeded, unknown target, `OnHandoff` deny) emit no
124	result. The run ends there with `RunFailed`, so the recorder's synthetic result is the
125	last event, directly after the call. This is the behaviour of today.
126	
127	### Remove the repeated-id deny
128	
129	- Delete the `open_call_ids` check in the `Authorization::Defer` arm (`agent.rs`).
130	- Delete `RunContext.open_call_ids`, `open_call_ids()`, `with_open_call_ids()` and their
131	  copies in `handoff_child` / `subagent_child` (`context.rs`). They are `pub(crate)` and
132	  have no other use, so this is not an API change. Delete the unit test
133	  `handoff_child_keeps_open_call_ids_and_subagent_child_clears_them`.
134	- `transfer_call_ids` stays: step 5 uses it.
135	
136	### Read-time repair in `project()` (G4, `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs`)
137	
138	The second spec challenge rejected a first version that moved every result to the end
139	of its "tool block". A tool-only model response makes no `AssistantMessage`
140	(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
141	LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
142	in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
143	results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.
144	
145	**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
146	transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
147	`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
148	`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`). The two places share only this boundary scan
149	in one private helper. (`transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward
150	scan per call; `project()` must not call that part, or it becomes O(n × calls).)
151	
152	Scope: step 1 is exact for **sequential** logs. In a sequential log the scan stops at
153	the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at an earlier
154	`HandoffOccurred`, and `transition()` never records the non-transfer calls of a handoff
155	response. Two cases can put another call into the scanned run: a `ParallelAgent`
156	sibling's `ToolCalled` (the `OnHandoff` await is a yield point), and a run whose new
157	input ends with a `ToolCall` item. G4 does not support these cases (same limit as G3).
158	
159	**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
160	the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
161	with call id `x` closes:
162	
163	1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
164	2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.
165	
166	Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
167	The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,

169	the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
170	non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.
171	
172	**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list

177	**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
178	still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call

4	//! (SMA-568).
5	//!
6	//! Five properties are enforced per invocation:
7	//!
8	//! 1. A `target:` argument is present at all ([`TargetArg::Absent`] fails).
9	//! 2. It is a string literal, not a computed expression
10	//!    ([`TargetArg::NonLiteral`] fails) — a computed target satisfies
11	//!    coverage but cannot be shape-checked, which is exactly how an event
12	//!    could be routed out of the namespace invisibly.

18	//!    in the file — the scanner keys on `ident !` and cannot see an

128	### Bedrock — `paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`
129	
130	Reached as `paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel` behind the `bedrock`
131	feature. Covers the **Converse streaming API** — tool use and multi-turn
132	conversations across Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Amazon Titan, Meta Llama,
133	Mistral, and Cohere model families hosted on AWS Bedrock. Structured output
134	(forced-tool synthesis) is supported on Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, and
135	Mistral; Titan, Llama, and Cohere degrade to plain text responses.
136	
137	> **Disambiguation:** this is the Bedrock *Converse model provider*. It is
138	> distinct from `paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore`, which is the Bedrock
139	> *AgentCore runtime* host — a separate crate implementing the AgentCore
140	> container contract; see [Runtimes](./runtimes.md).
141	
142	#### Construction
143	
144	The simplest path loads AWS configuration from the standard credential chain:
145	
146	```rust,ignore
147	use paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel;
148	
149	let model = BedrockModel::from_env("anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0").await?;
150	```
151	
152	`from_env` is `async` because it may fetch IMDS or SSO tokens. The credential
153	chain is **lazy** — auth failures surface at `invoke()` time, not here.
154	
155	For explicit configuration, use the synchronous builder:
156	
157	```rust,ignore
158	use aws_config::BehaviorVersion;
159	use paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel;
160	
161	let sdk_cfg = aws_config::defaults(BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
162	    .region(aws_config::Region::new("us-east-1"))
163	    .load()
164	    .await;
165	
166	let model = BedrockModel::converse("amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")
167	    .sdk_config(&sdk_cfg)
168	    .build()?;
169	```
170	
171	`BedrockModel::converse(id)` returns a `BedrockModelBuilder`; `build()` yields a
172	`Result<BedrockModel, BuildError>`. You can also inject a pre-constructed
173	`aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::Client` via `.client(c)` for full control.
174	
175	#### Family-gated structured output
176	
177	The `bedrock` provider detects the model family from the Bedrock model ID. For
178	families that support Bedrock's forced-tool-choice — `Anthropic`, `AmazonNova`,
179	and `Mistral` — `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` is synthesized as a hidden tool
180	call: the model is forced to invoke an internal reserved tool whose input schema
181	is the user-supplied JSON Schema, and the result is returned as a structured
182	JSON response. For other families (`AmazonTitan`, `Llama`, `Cohere`, `Unknown`)
183	a `JsonSchema` format degrades silently to a text response.
184	
185	Cross-region inference profile prefixes (`us.`, `eu.`, `ap.`, `apac.`) are
186	stripped before family detection, so model IDs such as
187	`us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0` are correctly identified as
188	`Anthropic`.
189	
190	Reasoning content surfaced by the model (e.g. extended-thinking responses from
191	Claude) is delivered as `ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta` in the stream — no extra
192	configuration is required on this provider.
193	
194	#### Tool-input schema rewriter
195	
196	Bedrock's Converse API validator rejects JSON Schemas containing `$ref`/`$defs`,
197	`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, or meta-keywords such as `$schema`, `format`, and
198	`examples`. The crate exposes `rewrite_tool_schema(schema, Ruleset::Strict)`,
199	which runs automatically on every tool spec before the request is sent:
200

`AnthropicModel::messages(id)` returns an `AnthropicModelBuilder`; `build()`
yields a `Result<AnthropicModel, BuildError>`.

### Bedrock — `paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`

Reached as `paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel` behind the `bedrock`
feature. Covers the **Converse streaming API** — tool use and multi-turn
conversations across Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Amazon Titan, Meta Llama,
Mistral, and Cohere model families hosted on AWS Bedrock. Structured output
(forced-tool synthesis) is supported on Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, and
Mistral; Titan, Llama, and Cohere degrade to plain text responses.

> **Disambiguation:** this is the Bedrock *Converse model provider*. It is
> distinct from `paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore`, which is the Bedrock
> *AgentCore runtime* host — a separate crate implementing the AgentCore
> container contract; see [Runtimes](./runtimes.md).

#### Construction

The simplest path loads AWS configuration from the standard credential chain:

```rust,ignore
use paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel;

let model = BedrockModel::from_env("anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0").await?;
```

`from_env` is `async` because it may fetch IMDS or SSO tokens. The credential
chain is **lazy** — auth failures surface at `invoke()` time, not here.

For explicit configuration, use the synchronous builder:

```rust,ignore
use aws_config::BehaviorVersion;
use paigasus_helikon::bedrock::BedrockModel;

let sdk_cfg = aws_config::defaults(BehaviorVersion::v2026_11_17())
    .region(aws_config::Region::new("us-east-1"))
    .load()
    .await;

let model = BedrockModel::converse("amazon.nova-pro-v1:0")
    .sdk_config(&sdk_cfg)
    .build()?;
```

`BedrockModel::converse(id)` returns a `BedrockModelBuilder`; `build()` yields a
`Result<BedrockModel, BuildError>`. You can also inject a pre-constructed
`aws_sdk_bedrockruntime::Client` via `.client(c)` for full control.

#### Family-gated structured output

The `bedrock` provider detects the model family from the Bedrock model ID. For
families that support Bedrock's forced-tool-choice — `Anthropic`, `AmazonNova`,
and `Mistral` — `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` is synthesized as a hidden tool
call: the model is forced to invoke an internal reserved tool whose input schema
is the user-supplied JSON Schema, and the result is returned as a structured
JSON response. For other families (`AmazonTitan`, `Llama`, `Cohere`, `Unknown`)
a `JsonSchema` format degrades silently to a text response.

Cross-region inference profile prefixes (`us.`, `eu.`, `ap.`, `apac.`) are
stripped before family detection, so model IDs such as
`us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0` are correctly identified as
`Anthropic`.

Reasoning content surfaced by the model (e.g. extended-thinking responses from
Claude) is delivered as `ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta` in the stream — no extra
configuration is required on this provider.

#### Tool-input schema rewriter

Bedrock's Converse API validator rejects JSON Schemas containing `$ref`/`$defs`,
`oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, or meta-keywords such as `$schema`, `format`, and
`examples`. The crate exposes `rewrite_tool_schema(schema, Ruleset::Strict)`,
which runs automatically on every tool spec before the request is sent:

- `$ref` references are inlined recursively (cycles and excessive depth are
  terminated with a permissive `{"type": "object"}`).
- `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` combinators (e.g. serde-generated tagged enums) are
  collapsed into a flat `object` whose `properties` union the variants' fields
  and whose shared tag key becomes an `enum` of variant names.
- Unsupported meta-keywords are stripped.

This means schemars-derived schemas for tagged enums and generic structs pass
Bedrock's validator without any manual schema adjustment.

#### Credentials and TLS

The provider uses the standard AWS credential chain via `aws-config`
(environment variables, `~/.aws/credentials`, SSO, IMDS, ECS task role, …) and
the `aws-lc-rs` TLS backend — the same crypto provider the workspace already
uses via `reqwest`/`async-openai`. Do not enable the AWS SDK `ring` feature
alongside this crate; a second `CryptoProvider` panics.

> Model ids are illustrative — swap them for any model your account can reach
> if the provider rejects the id.

### Gemini — `paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini`

Reached as `paigasus_helikon::gemini::GeminiModel` behind the `gemini` feature.
Covers the **Gemini streaming API** — tool use, structured output, and
multi-turn conversations against Google's Gemini model family. Structured output
is **native** (`responseSchema`) — the provider does not use forced-tool synthesis.

> **Note:** Gemini rejects requests that combine structured output with active
> function calling. If your `ModelRequest` sets a `ResponseFormat::JsonObject`
> or `ResponseFormat::JsonSchema` while `tools` is non-empty **or** `tool_choice`
> is anything other than `None`, the provider returns a conflict error before
> sending.
